events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip was RydeTAXI (metered), so a route deviation would feed directly into the fare, and the meter does show a detour: actual 12.4 km vs optimal 9.8 km, +2.6 km (+26%) [F1], with one off-route segment 09:03–09:11 of 3.97 km where the optimal route covers only 1.80 km, adding 2.18 km and reaching up to 1040 m from the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 provides that every such segment must be examined against RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [RD-1]. The rider's denial of consent [F7, F8] is consistent with the record — there is no in-app chat at all [F7] — so no RD-5 or RD-3 branch could have excused the segment; but neither is needed here.

RD-4(a) is satisfied for that segment: an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 08:44 on the Tampines Expressway (towards PIE) after the Punggol Road Exit, i.e. on the optimal route (0 m from it), before the segment began at 09:03 [F12, F3], and the Tampines Expressway speed band was recorded as band 1 (0–9 km/h) covering 08:47–09:03 [F9], corroborating the reported blockage at the time the driver diverted [RD-4]. The driver's account of an accident and blocked lanes on that expressway [F8] is therefore corroborated by the system traffic records rather than being a bare assertion, and the segment is exempt under RD-4(a) with no_action for it [RD-4].

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, there are no non-exempt segments to compute under RD-2; the amount is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4097/km = 0 km × $1.4097/km = $0.00, so the metered fare of $29.26 (base $3.90 + distance $17.48 for 12.40 km + time $6.41 for 24.7 min + platform $1.47) stands [F4, F6, RD-2]. The excess-distance figure of $3.61 is the billed consequence of that exempt segment, not a recoverable overcharge [F4, RD-2].

The RD-6 account flag does not arise: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (route: 0), so the profile condition (upheld route disputes ≥ 1, making this a "repeated" breach) is not met, and this is the only clause that could trigger flag_account [F15, RD-6]. Rider-side dispute history (2 disputes, 0 upheld) is not used to decide anything [F14, RD-6].

The non-metered branches (FARE-1, RD-3(c)) are not engaged — this was a metered RydeTAXI trip with a published meter breakdown and no add-on beyond the published platform fee [F6, FARE-1].

Safety screen: I read the complaint ("The driver left the route the app showed and the meter was higher than the estimate. I never agreed to any change."), the driver's statement ("There was an accident on Tampines Expressway ahead, lanes were blocked, so I went round it. The extra distance was unavoidable."), and the chat record (none) [F7, F8]. I find no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the exchange is a pure routing/fare disagreement — so the screen is none [SAFE-1, SAFE-2].

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — a measured off-route segment with start/end times and distances, an incident fact on the replaced stretch with a timestamp preceding the segment, speed-band corroboration, the fare breakdown with the trip's distance fare and distance km, and a complete (empty) chat record; no record is missing, so no gap is named [F3, F4, F6, F7, F12]. events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute about the fare on this RydeTAXI trip and found no refund is due.

Your trip was metered, and the meter did show a longer route than the app's route. However, that stretch was covered by a documented accident on the expressway you were travelling on: the accident was reported before the driver diverted, and traffic speed records at the time confirm the road was blocked. Under our rules, a diversion around a recorded accident is exempt, so the metered fare stands.

There's no change to your account, and no further action is needed.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare dispute raised on this RydeTAXI trip. The outcome: no action against you and no amount deducted.

Two facts decided it. The accident on the expressway ahead of you was recorded in official traffic data before you diverted, and the traffic speed band at that time showed the road was effectively blocked. That makes the diversion an exempt one, so the metered fare stands and no overcharge is owed.

There's no mark on your account and no flag from this case, so nothing changes for you. No further action is needed on your side.

We reviewed your dispute about the fare on this RydeTAXI trip and found no refund is due.

Your trip was metered, and the meter did show a longer route than the app's route. However, that stretch was covered by a documented accident on the expressway you were travelling on: the accident was reported before the driver diverted, and traffic speed records at the time confirm the road was blocked. Under our rules, a diversion around a recorded accident is exempt, so the metered fare stands.

There's no change to your account, and no further action is needed.
